newsitem.title: GERMANY: WestLB raises earnings estimates for BASF.
newsitem.headline: WestLB raises earnings estimates for BASF.

text.p: German bank WestLB on Friday said it had raised its earnings estimates for chemicals group BASF AG, predicting that stronger earnings in the oil and gas business would help boost overall revenues.
Analysts at the bank predicted even stronger earnings growth than did BASF executives, well known for downplaying predictions.

WestLB said the group's dividend could rise to 1.90 marks for 1997 from 1.70 marks for 1996. It also raised its earnings per share to 5.02 marks from 4.90 marks for the current year. For 1998 the group expects earnings per share at 5.05 marks.
The group held an analyst meeting on Thursday, one day after its news conference. Analysts said they welcomed BASF's decision to offer more detailed results information.
Last year BASF posted sales of 48.8 billion marks and pre-tax profit of 4.4 billion marks while the DVFA earnings per share jumped to 4.40 marks from 3.77 marks.
BASF shares had already benefitted from the company's upbeat outlook and were buoyed further by analysts' comments.
After the shares closed floor trade up 2.15 marks at 63.65 marks some gains were lost in after hour trading with shares slipping to 63.25 marks.
